feedback: Approved. The candidate is the iteration 9 design unchanged: kp 2.5, kd 1.2, ki 0, base_speed 1.2, 16 mm sensors at x = -0.03 to +0.03 m, weights -2 to 2, mass 0.6 kg, body 0.14 m, wheel track 0.14 m, line_loss last_direction. Iteration 9 is the best raced design at 917.47. Iteration 10 raised kp to 2.75 and scored lower (902.2), with slalom finishes back to 16/20 and line-loss events up to 0.35, so kp has passed its useful point. Iteration 8 showed kd is saturated (kd 1.5 gave 907.6, no gain). Iteration 7 showed kp 2.0 loses turn authority (slalom 11/20, 0.6 line-loss events). Nothing new is tested here, so the result on the held-back track is not predicted. Because this is the final iteration, another review-and-revision round would risk the delivery, and no variant has beaten iteration 9 on the development tracks. The slalom off-track exits (3 to 4 of 20, about 0.15 line-loss events per run) remain the main gap. If a later race is ever run on this design, check the failing runs for line_loss_events versus max_error to tell turn-authority loss from overshoot.
requested_changes: No change for this final submission. Keep kp 2.5, kd 1.2, ki 0, base_speed 1.2 and the iteration 9 geometry as raced (917.47).
For any future iteration: if slalom line-loss events are above 0.15 on an unseen track, test ki 0.1 at kp 2.5 before raising kp again, since iteration 10 showed kp 2.75 is worse.
